name: apple-music-mcp
description: Search your music library and read its play history, through the Music app
long_description:
A local MCP server written in Swift that gives Claude access to the Music app on this Mac.

Music has no framework a separate process can use, so this server drives Music.app itself through Apple events. Music must be running, and the grant appears under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation.

The interesting part is what Music already records and rarely shows you: play counts, last played, skip counts, ratings, date added. Those come back as raw rows. This server computes no statistics and ranks nothing — the reading of the rows is Claude's job, where you can see it happen and argue with it.

Every result is bounded and says what it left out. Tracks, playlists and search results come one page at a time; when a result does not hold everything, its first lines say so and give the exact arguments that return the rest (limit and offset, or character_offset and max_characters for one track's record and lyrics). tracks_list and playlist_get read only the rows of the page, so every track can be reached however large the library. A search matches its query in this server, so it reads tracks to search them: it stops after 2000 tracks and says so, and genre, year_from, year_to and playlist_id narrow what it scans. A number outside its range is moved to the nearest allowed value, and the result says which one was used; a volume too is moved and reported. tracks_list takes from_date and to_date for the date a track was added.

Every call is bounded in time: reading stops after 40 seconds and the result says that it is partial, and a call that has not answered after 55 seconds is abandoned with an error that says so.

Nothing here removes a track or a playlist. add_to_playlist only ever appends, and refuses smart playlists, whose contents are the output of their rules. Because there is no way back, it takes a skip_duplicates option for the case that actually bites: retrying an add that had already gone through.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple Inc.

tools.name: music_status
tools.description: Reports whether Music is running and whether this server may drive it, and says exactly what to enable and where if it may not. Also shows the bounds in force: how far a search scans, how many rows a page holds and how long a call may take.

tools.name: now_playing
tools.description: Returns the current track with its library row, how far into it playback has reached, the player state, the volume, and the playlist it is coming from.

tools.name: music_search
tools.description: Finds tracks, albums, artists or playlists whose text matches a query, one page at a time; limit and offset reach the rest. It scans at most 2000 tracks and says so when it stopped there; genre, year_from, year_to and playlist_id narrow the scan.

tools.name: tracks_list
tools.description: Returns library rows one page at a time, with the fields Music stores about a track: play count and last played, skip count, rating, favourite flag, date added and more. limit and offset reach every row, however large the library; from_date and to_date bound the date added.

tools.name: playlists_list
tools.description: Lists the playlists one page at a time, each with its id, track count, total time, and whether add_to_playlist can append to it; limit and offset reach the rest.

tools.name: playlist_get
tools.description: Returns a playlist's details and one page of its tracks as raw rows, the same shape tracks_list returns; limit and offset reach every track.

tools.name: track_get
tools.description: Given one id, returns everything Music stores about that track, comment and lyrics included, one window at a time when it is long. Given several (up to 20), returns each record with its lyrics shortened to 500 characters.

tools.name: create_playlist
tools.description: Creates a new, empty playlist in Music. Refuses a name already in use.

tools.name: add_to_playlist
tools.description: Appends up to 100 tracks to an existing playlist. It only ever adds: nothing already in the playlist is removed, replaced or reordered. Pass skip_duplicates=true to leave out ids the playlist already holds — worth setting when retrying an add that may already have succeeded.

tools.name: music_control
tools.description: CHANGES WHAT IS CURRENTLY PLAYING on this Mac: starts or pauses playback, skips to the next or previous track, or sets the system music volume. The effect is immediate and audible to whoever is at the machine.
